Q: How to listen to CTRL key in C? A:

I can say your code works correctly for me on standard terminal for MATE (mate-terminal) and with WezTerm but it makes problem with xterm and Alacritty

Problem can be because some terminals catch Ctrl+Q (and Ctrl+S) for own use.

If I set

    new1.c_iflag &= ~IXON;

then it work for me.

Usually it is together with IXOFF

    new1.c_iflag &= ~(IXON|IXOFF);

pty - What is the difference between IXON and IXOFF tty attributes? - Unix & Linux Stack Exchange

Manual for termios:

IXON   Enable XON/XOFF flow control on output.

IXOFF  Enable XON/XOFF flow control on input.

There is also some info about Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+S

VSTART (021, DC1, Ctrl-Q) Start character (START).  Restarts
       output stopped by the Stop character.  Recognized when IXON
       is set, and then not passed as input.

VSTOP  (023, DC3, Ctrl-S) Stop character (STOP).  Stop output
       until Start character typed.  Recognized when IXON is set,
       and then not passed as input.

Q: How to prevent duplicate usernames in a Node.js chat room using Socket.io? A:

1. The Correct Way to Check for Duplicates

You should not iterate through the entire users array inside a loop for every incoming request. Instead, use a Map or a Set for O(1)O(1) constant-time lookup.

In Socket.io, the "source of truth" for who is in a room should be the server's memory (or a database/Redis store).

2. Should this be handled on the server? Yes, absolutely. You cannot trust the client. A malicious user can write their own script to bypass your validateUser function and send a join event with a duplicate name directly to your server.

3. How to properly stop the user

The server should perform the check before calling socket.join(). If the validation fails, use an acknowledgment callback to tell the client the attempt was rejected.

Q: Access values associated with a generic type in TypeScript A:

The issue is that TypeScript type parameters are erased entirely at runtime, so `T` in `foo<T>()` produces no JavaScript and you cannot read values from it.

To answer your second question first: no, the TypeScript compiler will not emit `foo(Bar.foo)` or `foo(1)` when it sees `foo<Bar, 1>()`. Type arguments are hints to the type checker only. Q: How to setup npm for private registry A:

Hey, I’m seeing an issue with the PDF viewer — it’s failing with a worker error (pdf.worker.mjs) and sometimes the file URL returns 404.

Could you please check if the worker setup is configured correctly on your side and also verify if the PDF URL is valid?

Issue: PDF Viewer Worker Failure & File Load Error

📌 Summary

We are encountering issues while rendering PDFs in the application. The PDF viewer is failing to load properly due to a worker configuration problem, and in some cases, the PDF file itself is not accessible.

⚠️ Errors Observed

  1. PDF Worker Error
Warning: Setting up fake worker.
Error: Setting up fake worker failed: Failed to resolve module specifier 'pdf.worker.mjs'

enter image description here

  1. File Load Error
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404

enter image description here

🧠 Understanding the Issue

  • The PDF viewer (PDF.js via react-pdf) requires a web worker (pdf.worker.mjs) to process PDF files efficiently.

  • Currently, the worker file is not being resolved correctly by the bundler (Vite/Webpack).

  • As a fallback, the system tries to use a fake worker, which also fails — resulting in the error.

Additionally:

  • Some PDF URLs are returning 404 errors, meaning the file is either:

    • Not available on the server

    • Incorrectly referenced

    • Not properly served via API/static path

Fix Worker Setup (Frontend)

import { pdfjs } from "react-pdf";
import worker from "pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker?url";

pdfjs.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = worker;

Verify Dependency

npm install pdfjs-dist

Fix PDF URL Issue

  • Validate API response for correct file URL

  • Ensure file is accessible via browser

  • Check backend/static file serving configuration

Expected Outcome

  • PDF loads without warnings

  • No fallback to fake worker

  • Improved performance (worker-based rendering)

  • No 404 errors for PDF files

Q: How to learn python with more practical approach A:

maybe find some problem on your computer and try to resolve it with Python.

e.g. rename files/images, sort them to subfolders, generate HTML with links to make preview, calculate size of all images, etc.

You may also create some dataset with own information and use it in Python - e.g everyday write in CSV you weight, and later use pandas to get stats, and matplotlib to display plot.
